_comment: Pinned upstream schema against review revision: 44 original vectors + 8 AirShelf-inspired synthetic vectors; not private seller data. kind selects variant/product validation.

vectors.note: minimal priced variant; no regression
transcribed from docs rest.md Blue Runner Pro search example
amount:0 keeps its released 'free' meaning
all-priced product keeps price_range required
the gap: baseline rejects with 'price' required
anonymous caller sees buyer_specific without price

UPDATED 2026-10-05: this is now the PROPOSED NORMATIVE representation of a resolved buyer_specific response (point 3 of maintainer feedback), not merely one of two unresolved interpretations — mode MUST remain buyer_specific when a price is present. Old validators see a normal priced variant (forward-safe).
mixed product may omit price_range
all-on-request product omits price_range
old validators cannot see the conflict (pricing ignored); new schema rejects it
explicit-on-request vs accidentally-missing stay distinguishable

mode is an open vocabulary (point 1 of maintainer feedback) — unknown mode 'negotiable' with a numeric price validates under proposed. Baseline's closed-enum behavior is unaffected (baseline ignores pricing entirely via additionalProperties, so it was already valid). Unaffected by the 2026-10-05 contract_only reversal.
fabricated range over zero priced variants rejected by both
list_price is a legitimate reference on an unpriced variant
unit_price is a per-unit selling price: banned with no-price modes
unit_price requires price to be present
priced buyer_specific variant may carry unit_price
baseline rejects the priceless variant; proposed permits list_price_range on mixed products
baseline rejects priceless variants; proposed rejects the list_price_range
Worker-C: pricing:null is an open extra under baseline; proposed requires an object — narrows
Worker-C: the bare-string shorthand sketched in #877 is rejected by both (baseline: price required; proposed: pricing must be an object)
Worker-C: pricing:{} is an open extra under baseline; proposed requires mode — narrows
Worker-C: unknown fields inside pricing stay open under proposed (only mode is a closed enum)

Worker-C: a mode is present but pricing is not an object (it's an array); baseline ignores it, proposed rejects the shape because pricing itself must be an object with a string mode — this narrowing is about the malformed OBJECT SHAPE, unrelated to the open-vocabulary change to mode's value space (point 1 of maintainer feedback only removed the enum constraint on the mode value, not the type:object/required:mode constraints on pricing itself) — narrows

mode is an open vocabulary — unknown mode 'negotiated' alongside a numeric price validates under proposed (safe-fallback behavior for unrecognized modes is a consumer/behavioral requirement, not a schema rejection). Unaffected by the 2026-10-05 contract_only reversal — this fixture does not involve contract_only.
Worker-C: unit_price requires price under both (proposed keeps the cross-cutting rule even with no marker)
Worker-C: mode public keeps the released price-requiredness (baseline: top-level required; proposed: conditional rule)

unknown future-looking mode 'auction_pending', no price. Baseline rejects (price is unconditionally required); proposed is valid via safe fallback — no rule constrains an unrecognized mode. (= unknown_mode_without_price vector.)

REVERSED 2026-10-05 (flip from the prior round): contract_only WITH a numeric price. Baseline accepts (pricing is an ignored additionalProperties extra, and price is present so the unconditional price-requiredness is satisfied). Proposed is now INVALID: contract_only was resolved as a genuinely unpriced state (the unresolved response to an un-entitled caller); an entitled caller's resolved price transitions to buyer_specific + price instead, per the selected working design. The prior round's relaxation (which made this VALID as an open-question data shape) is reverted — rule 1's 'forbid price' condition is restored to cover both quote_required and contract_only (= contract_only_with_price vector).
ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 2): public/general-price stranger. Anonymous caller sees the ordinary public catalog price.
ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 2): contract-gated stranger. Baseline rejects (price unconditionally required); proposed valid — contract_only is a genuinely unpriced state.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 3): NDA deployment case — buyer_specific + price + next_step:request_quote. A buyer may have a real catalog price and still be able to request a negotiated quote; next_step does not imply price must be absent and does not participate in the conditional price rules.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 4): orthogonality case — public + price + next_step:request_quote. A public price exists; the Business also accepts quote requests. Tests that the model is orthogonal rather than accidentally special-casing NDA pricing.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 5): MUST stay invalid — price is UCP's ordinary selling price; quote_required says no such usable price has been resolved. Baseline accepts (marker ignored, price present); proposed rejects via rule 1 (quote_required forbids price), unaffected by next_step.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (point 9): mixed product with one variant carrying a numeric price alongside an unrecognized pricing mode. Schema-valid shape (data shape only) -- the CONSUMER'S range computation safety for the unknown-mode variant is a behavioral rule documented in product.json prose/DESIGN.md, not something jsonschema can check.
ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 5, Scenario A, anonymous state): ordinary public catalog price, no pricing object. Valid under both; narrative pair with the resolved-state fixture below.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 5, Scenario A, resolved state): recognized buyer's negotiated price, mode buyer_specific retained alongside price (point 3's proposed normative behavior). Valid under both (baseline ignores pricing, price is present so price-requiredness is satisfied).

ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 5, Scenario B, anonymous state): no anonymous price exists; contract_only with no price, price_range correctly omitted. Baseline rejects (price and price_range are both unconditionally required); proposed valid.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 5, Scenario B, resolved state): the prototype's cleanest representation transitions contract_only -> buyer_specific + price on resolution; whether the resolved response should instead retain contract_only + price is an OPEN design question (not decided by this fixture). Valid under both.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 9/10): mixed product (A=$100, B=quote_required no price, C=$150) WITH a present price_range computed only over priced variants -> $100-$150, never zero-filled. Baseline rejects (variant B lacks the unconditionally-required price); proposed valid. Complements onrequest_product_mixed_norange.json, which tests the omit-range case rather than the compute-over-priced-subset case.

ADDED 2026-10-05 (feedback point 4/9/10): buyer_specific priced variants (A=$80, B=$110) producing a caller-specific price_range of $80-$110. Valid under both schemas (baseline ignores pricing; all variants carry price so price-requiredness/price_range-requiredness are satisfied) — flagged here because this price_range is subject to the SAME cache-isolation requirement as the underlying buyer-specific prices (point 4): a Platform MUST NOT reuse it for a different caller. This is a behavioral/cache requirement, not something the schema validation itself can check.
undisclosed protects NDA price-list membership; no price and no identity-linking promise
even a numeric amount alongside undisclosed is invalid; old clients can ignore the mode
reason cannot leak membership or pricing path
next_step cannot disclose quote-only versus price-list status
reference price cannot leak via a neutral response
two hidden variants have identical pricing mode; no price_range
no aggregate price when all variants are neutral
mixed anonymous catalog: public-only range with a neutral variant
